stem:
Meena dips one hand in a bowl of warm water and her other hand in a bowl of cool water for a minute. She then puts both hands together into a third bowl of water at room temperature.
To one hand the water feels warm and to the other it feels cool, but a thermometer in the third bowl shows one steady reading.
What does this activity show?

options.text: The water in the third bowl is both warm and cool at the same time.
Our sense of touch cannot always judge hotness or coldness reliably, so temperature must be measured with a thermometer.
The thermometer reading changes depending on which hand touches the bowl.
Warm water and cool water mix to make the thermometer stop working.

teacher.key_rationale: The same water feels different to the two hands because of their prior contact with warm and cool water, while the thermometer gives a single dependable reading. Hence touch is unreliable and temperature must be measured — option B.
